hypothesis: R238's five-position candidate passed all gates, but a five-stock equal-weight portfolio can be driven by one or two names. This round audits the actual engine trades from the frozen R238 candidate across 2022-2026 and tests whether the P&L is diversified across symbols and industries. It is a concentration audit, not a new alpha discovery.

execution.universe: historical non-financial HS300 membership; daily snapshots from 2022

gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full period
gates.C2: the single largest symbol's share of net P&L is at most 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is at most 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is at most 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the single largest symbol's share of validation gross profit is at most 35%
gates.C7: the largest industry's share of gross profit is at most 45%
gates.C8: the single largest symbol loss is at most 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All C gates must pass. A failure means the five-position candidate's P&L is too concentrated to justify even paper trading without additional diversification controls. No gate may be relaxed after seeing the audit.
known_limitations: Trade P&L amounts from two segments each start from 1,000,000 notional, so the audit is a contribution-share analysis, not a compounded-return decomposition.
Industry classification is a current snapshot, not historical PIT.
The audit describes concentration, not causality.
Passing concentration gates does not override the result-driven nature of the five-position choice.
